theme: All have sinned; justification by faith
readingInstruction: Read Romans 3:1-31. This chapter is the hinge of the letter. Read the verdict in 3:9-20 and then the great turn at 3:21, “But now.” Take your time with 3:21-26, one of the most important passages in the Bible.
settingTheScene: Paul has argued that Gentiles (chapter 1) and Jews (chapter 2) are all under God’s judgment. Chapter 3 begins with objections: if the Jews are guilty too, what advantage has the Jew? Does unbelief cancel God’s faithfulness? Paul answers briefly, then delivers the verdict on the whole human race. Then, like sunrise, the next section begins with “But now.” The righteousness of God has been manifested.
observation: “To begin with, the Jews were entrusted with the oracles of God” (3:2).
“For by works of the law no human being will be justified in his sight, since through the law comes knowledge of sin” (3:20).
“But now the righteousness of God has been manifested apart from the law, although the Law and the Prophets bear witness to it” (3:21).
“For all have sinned and fall short of the glory of God” (3:23).
“And are justified by his grace as a gift, through the redemption that is in Christ Jesus” (3:24).
“Whom God put forward as a propitiation by his blood, to be received by faith” (3:25).
“For we hold that one is justified by faith apart from works of the law” (3:28).
interpretation:
The Jews have a real advantage: they were entrusted with the oracles of God, the Scriptures. But possessing the Bible is not the same as obeying it. Does Israel’s unfaithfulness nullify God’s faithfulness? “By no means! Let God be true though every one were a liar.” God’s character is not at stake in human failure. Paul answers a twisted objection, “Why not do evil that good may come?” with a short, firm rejection.

Then he gathers a series of Old Testament quotations, mostly from the Psalms and Isaiah, into a portrait of universal sin: “None is righteous, no, not one; no one understands; no one seeks for God. All have turned aside… no one does good, not even one.” Throats are open graves, feet are swift to shed blood, and “there is no fear of God before their eyes.” The point is stated at verse 19: “so that every mouth may be stopped, and the whole world may be held accountable to God.” The law cannot save because it was never given for that purpose. “Through the law comes knowledge of sin.” It is a mirror, not a rescue.

Then, “But now.” These two words mark the biggest turn in Romans. “The righteousness of God has been manifested apart from the law, although the Law and the Prophets bear witness to it.” This is the new covenant fulfillment of the old. The righteousness comes “through faith in Jesus Christ for all who believe. For there is no distinction: for all have sinned and fall short of the glory of God, and are justified by his grace as a gift, through the redemption that is in Christ Jesus.”

Three words carry the weight. Justified: declared righteous in God’s courtroom. Grace: a free gift, not earned. Redemption: a slave market word for being bought back with a price. And then “whom God put forward as a propitiation by his blood, to be received by faith.” Propitiation means a sacrifice that satisfies God’s wrath. God himself provides it. Paul explains why: “This was to show God’s righteousness, because in his divine forbearance he had passed over former sins.” In the Old Testament, God forgave sin and seemed to overlook it. Now it is clear how he could do so justly: the cross. “So that he might be just and the justifier of the one who has faith in Jesus.” God is both just and the one who justifies the ungodly. That is the miracle.

Boasting is excluded. If salvation were by works, we could boast. It is by faith, so all glory goes to God. And this faith does not cancel the law; it upholds it, since Christ fulfilled it.
connection: Psalm 14:1-3 and 53:1-3 describe human sin. Psalm 5:9, 10:7, 36:1, 140:3, and Isaiah 59:7-8 are quoted in verses 13-18. Leviticus 16 describes the Day of Atonement and the mercy seat, the background of “propitiation.” Isaiah 53:4-6, 10-12 gives the Servant bearing sin. Proverbs 17:15 says that justifying the wicked is an abomination to the LORD, which makes the cross necessary. 2 Corinthians 5:21 says he became sin for us, so that in him we might become the righteousness of God. Galatians 2:16 and Ephesians 2:8-9 repeat the point.
application:
Memorize Romans 3:23-24. They hold the whole gospel in two verses.

Ask whether you are secretly trying to earn God’s favor. Let boasting be excluded today.

Thank God for the cross, where he is both just and the justifier.
prayerPrompts: Confess where you have fallen short of his glory.
Thank God for justifying you by grace as a gift.
Thank Jesus for the redemption that is in him.
